beats.narration_en: Same crash. Same seatbelt. Only one car has an airbag.
The belt holds your chest but your head keeps going
and without an airbag it hits the steering wheel.
A crash sensor feels the car slow down in the first few milliseconds
and decides in an instant that this is a real crash.
It fires a tiny igniter inside the steering wheel
which sets off a gas generator.
The gas splits the cover along a hidden seam
and fills the folded bag in about thirty milliseconds.
Here is the clever part. The bag has holes in it.
As your head sinks in the gas escapes through the vents
so the bag slows you down gently instead of bouncing you back.
That is why you should sit back from the wheel and always wear your belt.
